justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: online submissions via Web Portal (SPA) and Claim Submission REST API (R-01), adjuster processing via Adjuster Workspace (R-02), and phased migration via API Gateway / Router and Feature Flag Router Component (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: To beat the 5s mainframe latency (R-05), Claim Processing Dashboard uses TanStack Query caching and optimistic updates, while asynchronous decoupling via Integration & Sync Engine and local reads from Azure SQL Database ensure sub-2s response times.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability with Identity Provider and Legacy Mainframe is addressed via Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) and mTLS/ExpressRoute. However, explicit mechanisms to avoid conflicting with the strict 23:00-05:00 mainframe nightly batch window are not fully detailed.
justifications.usability: Customers and brokers are served by Web Portal (SPA) with local form persistence (Dexie.js), while Claims Adjusters receive the dedicated Adjuster Workspace featuring optimistic dashboard updates and offline draft management.
justifications.reliability: Strict consistency (R-04) is enforced by Idempotency & Reconciliation Worker, persistent transaction tracking in Azure SQL Database, Azure Service Bus dead-lettering, and Circuit Breaker & Fallback Handler in API Gateway / Router.
justifications.security: Meets R-07 via Token Validation Middleware and Identity Provider integration. PII Protection Enclave, Azure Key Vault tokenization, mTLS, and an append-only Audit & Activity Trail Service provide robust data security and auditability.
justifications.maintainability: Dynamic Route Dispatcher and Feature Flag Router Component enable one-day rollbacks (R-06). Clear separation exists across services, though using disparate stacks (YARP, Kafka, Azure Service Bus, Cosmos DB) poses challenges for a team with little cloud experience.
justifications.portability: Deployments span hybrid on-premises and Azure West Europe as required, but deep coupling to proprietary Azure platform services (Azure Container Apps, Azure Service Bus, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Static Web Apps) limits portability outside Azure.

PERF-01.justification: TanStack Query and optimistic caching in the Adjuster Workspace help mask latency on subsequent interactions, but the architecture lacks an explicit read-through cache or read-model synchronization in Claims Core Service to guarantee cold loads under 2 seconds when reading 5-second mainframe data.
sensitivity_points: Client-side caching sensitivity during cold loads of unmigrated hybrid records
Synchronous calls across the hybrid interconnect directly impact page render latency
tradeoffs: Optimistic UI updates improve perceived responsiveness at the cost of eventual consistency

PERF-02.justification: Submissions are decoupled asynchronously via Azure Container Apps, Azure SQL, and Azure Service Bus/Kafka in the Integration & Sync Engine. The Anti-Corruption Layer buffers traffic, fully insulating the legacy mainframe batch processing window from online traffic spikes.
sensitivity_points: Message broker queue buffering capacity during sustained peak submission periods
tradeoffs: Asynchronous submission ingestion increases throughput while deferring mainframe consistency

AVAIL-01.justification: Online claims are captured in Azure SQL and held reliably in Azure Service Bus Premium topics within the Integration & Sync Engine while the mainframe is offline during batch windows. Events are forwarded via the ACL once connectivity resumes.
sensitivity_points: Durability and partition limits of Azure Service Bus Premium during batch windows
tradeoffs: Decoupled availability trades immediate mainframe acknowledgment for continuous customer ingestion

AVAIL-02.justification: The Integration & Sync Engine contains a dedicated Idempotency & Reconciliation Worker with state tracking in Azure SQL and DLQ monitoring, ensuring deduplication, transaction hashing, and state reconciliation across failed or partial synchronization events without duplicate processing.
sensitivity_points: Precision of idempotency hash generation across partial payload sync retries
tradeoffs: Strict idempotency checks add database lookup overhead to every synchronization payload

MOD-01.justification: YARP dynamic route dispatching combined with Spring Cloud Feature Management enables claim-type-based routing between modern services and the legacy mainframe. Reverting a migration involves toggling a feature flag or route config within minutes without code redeployments.
sensitivity_points: Feature flag state consistency between API Gateway and Claims Core Service
tradeoffs: Dynamic dual-routing adds operational complexity to the gateway layer

MOD-02.justification: User interfaces interact purely with the modern API Gateway and frontend workspace shell. Decommissioning the mainframe only requires updating router dispatching and retiring the ACL sync engine; client applications require no changes or rewrites.
sensitivity_points: Abstraction purity of the API Gateway contracts shielding clients from backend changes
tradeoffs: Facade layers introduce slight routing overhead to preserve client UI stability

SEC-01.justification: The API Gateway verifies OIDC/OAuth tokens and Claims Core enforces domain rules, while Audit & Activity Trail Service captures cryptographic audit logs. However, explicit multi-tenant broker-to-customer ownership validation logic is not detailed at the component level.
sensitivity_points: Granular broker-customer authorization claims validation inside service handlers
tradeoffs: Detailed real-time authorization checks slightly increase submission processing latency

SEC-02.justification: Centralized authentication through Azure Active Directory allows immediate access revocation via token invalidation across SPA and Adjuster workspaces. However, propagating access removal to the legacy mainframe within 15 minutes depends on external AD synchronization not detailed in the architecture.
sensitivity_points: OAuth token lifetime and revocation propagation speed across hybrid identity providers
tradeoffs: Short-lived access tokens improve revocation speed but increase token refresh traffic
